speaker: Kimi K3
text: HONASA's operating margin has more than doubled from 5.9% to 13.2% in five quarters while revenue grew 27% YoY — that's real operating leverage, not just top-line fluff. Six straight EPS beats of 15-50% with 11 of 16 analysts rating it a buy gives the momentum a fundamental floor. The stock's only 11.8% off its all-time high after a 66.8% YTD run, so the easy money's made; the 2024 drawdown of -42% shows what happens when growth disappoints. For the Rs 10,000 account, six shares at ~Rs 1,582 costs ~Rs 38 round-trip plus 20% STCG tax — you need a 24% net move just to break even on costs before compounding starts.

On Zerodha, buying Reliance (RELIANCE.NS) in a delivery account costs about Rs 38 in total charges (brokerage 0, STT 0.1 %, exchange 0.59 %, SEBI 0.02 %, stamp duty 1.5 %, GST 0.11 % and DP 15.93 %). That’s a 0.38 % round‑trip cost. If you sell within a year you’ll hit the 20 % short‑term equity tax on the gain, so you need roughly a 24 % net move just to break even on costs.

For cars and battery names you could look at Maruti Suzuki (MARUTI.NS) or Tata Power (TATAPOWER.NS) – they’re larger, less volatile than pure‑play auto or battery stocks and offer steadier compounding, but they still won’t deliver 10× in a month without leverage or options.

Bottom line: a $10 IPO allotment is a lottery, Reliance costs ~0.4 % plus tax, and car/battery picks are safer but slower.

speaker: GLM
text: Muse is right to be wary, and I'll go further: NYKAA's Diwali crowd is the trade to fade, not follow — October has a -7.13% median over five years, up only 40% of the time, the operating margin is a thin 5.3%, and with Fed minutes flagging another hike, high-multiple consumer names get hit first. On the tape, PENG at RSI 74.7 on 6.4x normal volume is exactly the hype I'd avoid, while TITAN.NS at RSI 31.5 and GLAXO.NS down 4.9% in five days are the oversold quality nobody's talking about — that's where mean reversion actually pays. And for your cars-and-batteries ask, client: the crowd pays up for EV stories, but the odds live in the ignored names, and even then a 10x takes years of compounding, not one festive season.

text: GLM is right to point toward oversold quality; chasing festive hype in NYKAA.NS or PENG is how you lose the 10x goal to volatility.
